A1.justification: Both complete, readable 19-page PDFs describe TEAL. Their main sections, Algorithm 1, Figures 1–10, Tables 1–9, and Appendices A.1–A.2 can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original activation analyses, language-modeling and downstream-task evaluations, GPU speed measurements, and ablations. Appendix A includes empirical error comparisons and detailed task results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical studies in Sections 4–5 and Appendix A, including accuracy, decoding speed, quantization, and sparsification analyses.

M1.justification: Magnitude thresholding, Algorithm 1's greedy optimization, and the sparse kernel remain unchanged. Removing the introductory phrase about layer-dependent thresholds and clarifying equal block-level targets do not alter the procedure specified in Sections 4.2–4.3.

E1.justification: Both versions use C4 for activation analysis and WikiText, MMLU, ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, GSM8K, PiQA, and WinoGrande for evaluation. Quantization, prefill, and batched sparsification scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: CATS and ReLUfication in the relevant accuracy comparisons, DejaVu and torch.matmul in kernel benchmarking, and the GPT-Fast dense baseline in end-to-end timing. Uniform-versus-greedy comparisons are also retained.

E3.justification: The 128 WikiText samples, 2048-token context, 512-token evaluation window, task shot counts, prefill treatment, and timing configurations are unchanged. Both versions explicitly specify M = 10 calibration samples; correcting a conflicting factor in the cost calculation does not establish a changed calibration budget.

E4.justification: Sections 5.3–5.4 retain the same quantization, input-versus-output sparsity, greedy-versus-uniform allocation, layer sparsifiability, prefill, and batch-size analyses. Appendix A.1 retains the same theoretical-versus-empirical error comparison.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates and averages across tasks. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9 and all plotted results are unchanged, including the reported maximum decoding speedups of 1.53× and 1.8×. The corrected cost-calculation factor leaves the reported total of 9,800 forward passes unchanged and introduces no revised experimental outcome.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 corrects the numerical cost calculation from 16 × 7² / 0.05 = 9,800 to 10 × 7² / 0.05 = 9,800, resolving an arithmetic inconsistency. The complexity order, sparsification definitions, and all Appendix A.1 assumptions, lemmas, theorem, and proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of training-free model-wide activation sparsity, minimal degradation at 40–50% sparsity, practical decoding speedups, and compatibility with weight quantization.

C2.justification: Interpretations of activation distributions, input sparsity, layer sensitivity, attention sinks, and quantization compatibility are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same applicability to resource-constrained inference and limitations at larger batch sizes.

D1.justification: The calibration-cost documentation is made consistent with the already stated M = 10 by correcting the multiplier from 16 to 10. Sample length, step size, kernel implementation, hardware, timing information, and the project code link otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 lists conference and preprint records for the already cited CATS work as Lee et al. (2024a,b), replacing the single bibliographic record in v1. This does not introduce a distinct comparison method or change TEAL's positioning relative to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies the distinction between Transformer blocks and individual matrix layers, rephrases the common block-level sparsity assignment, trims an introductory clause, and adjusts citation formatting and CATS records. It also removes the acknowledgments; the scientific section structure is retained.

P2.justification: Removing the acknowledgments and revising the bibliography causes limited page reflow and a slight shift of Figure 10 within page 16. All figures, table structures, captions, axes, and legends are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves the inconsistent multiplier in the calibration-cost calculation and clarifies block-versus-layer terminology, improving internal consistency and readability. The experiments, claims, and appendix proofs remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
